## Module overview

Figures 1-3 and Supplementary Materials. We use our knowledge of the methods to analyze the first set of figures (Figures 1-3 and S1-9), learning about the findings and implications and thinking critically about the data and assumptions.

## Learning objectives

By the end of this module, you should be able to:

- Analyze the research findings shared by the authors.
- Summarize each figure, noting assumptions and implications.
- Discuss the findings of this study with peers.

## Module to-do list

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
checklist("module-4-todo", ["Review the Delftia background before the first session", "Complete the in-class activity and submit individually", "Summarize your assigned figure(s) using the Data Analysis Sheet (DAS) template"])
```

## Return to the article

Review the first three figures of the article and download the Supplementary Materials.

## Data Analysis Sheet (DAS)

For each figure panel record: **question**, **methods**, **controls**, **readout**, **result**, **assumptions**, **implications**.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
quiz("m4q1", "What should you identify first when analyzing a figure?", ["The authors' conclusion", "What the axes and legend show", "The journal impact factor", "The references"], 1, "Start from what is plotted.")
```

## My figure summary

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
notes("m4-figure", "Figure number, controls, readout, finding, assumptions, implications.")
```

## Reflect

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
notes("m4-reflect", "Do the data support the authors' claims so far?")
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
quiz("m4q2", "Which item belongs on a Data Analysis Sheet?", ["Only the final conclusion", "Question, methods, controls, readout, result, assumptions, implications", "The reference list", "Only the figure title"], 1, "The DAS walks through every part of a figure.")
```

::: {.takeaways}
### Key takeaways
- Start from what is plotted: axes, legend, controls.
- Record assumptions and implications, not only results.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
Article: Huang et al. (2023), *Delftia tsuruhatensis* TC1 symbiont suppresses malaria transmission by anopheline mosquitoes, *Science*. <https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adf8141>
:::
